long_biography.plain_text:
Mark Johnson had spent about twenty years with one technology company when remote meetings changed how he could work. He and his wife had long wanted to take their young daughters sailing, so they rented out their house and moved aboard after buying a large sailing boat in 2020. Their voyage began on the northeastern United States coast and continued south toward the Caribbean. Johnson kept consulting throughout, using a laptop and changing connectivity arrangements as the boat moved between harbours and open water.

That arrangement offered more time together as a family without ending his professional routine. Calls across different networks required planning, particularly when a delayed connection made group conversations awkward. The account identifies him as an American consultant but does not name the company, explain his position or document his stake in it. Nor does it establish whether the working arrangement continued after the voyage. The sailing episode is unusually vivid, yet it cannot by itself explain the origin or present scale of his wealth.
